scope: Primary-source review, not a claim of exhaustive worldwide coverage or first application

papers.title: Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I
papers.reading_depth: introduction excerpt only; PDF/browser challenge blocked full inspection
papers.model: Unitary representations and systems of imprimitivity of locally compact groups
papers.mapping: Induced-module decomposition motivates keeping full carrier modules, not deleting the complementary sector. The finite S3 calculation here is independently proved, not attributed to an uninspected theorem in this source.

papers.title: A group-theoretic approach to fast matrix multiplication
papers.reading_depth: abstract, Theorem 2.3 and its coefficient-extraction proof inspected
papers.locators: Theorem 2.3, PDF p. 4; group-algebra representation decomposition in Section 4
papers.model: Algebraic field-operation model; matrix product embedded in a finite group algebra
papers.mapping: Literal coefficient separation gives a model for checking that nominal independent jobs remain independent after packing. Group-algebra multiplication is not a free operation in our RAM model.

papers.authors: Henry Cohn; Robert Kleinberg; Balazs Szegedy; Christopher Umans
papers.title: Group-theoretic algorithms for matrix multiplication
papers.reading_depth: abstract, Definition 5.1, Theorems 5.3/5.5 and proof openings inspected
papers.model: Independent matrix products embedded by simultaneous triple-product property
papers.mapping: The simultaneous collision condition is stronger than separate packing of each job. It motivates checking cross-input terms of the actual dirty-target block rather than counting dependent outputs.

papers.authors: Ankit Garg; Leonid Gurvits; Rafael Oliveira; Avi Wigderson
papers.title: Operator scaling: theory and applications
papers.reading_depth: abstract; singularity equivalences; capacity bound and proof; bit-complexity organization inspected
papers.model: Rational matrix pencils in free noncommuting variables; completely positive operator capacity
papers.mapping: Noncommutative rank can expose matrix-valued encodings that scalar coefficients miss. Positive rank in a free skew field does not enforce our Clifford-group relations or supply a paid-call word.

papers.authors: Gabor Ivanyos; Youming Qiao; K. V. Subrahmanyam
papers.title: Constructive noncommutative rank computation is in deterministic polynomial time
papers.reading_depth: abstract; witness/blow-up setup; Section 5.1 proof; Section 6 reduction proof inspected
papers.model: Matrix spaces over fields, constructive rank witnesses and shrunk-subspace certificates
papers.mapping: A useful discovery algorithm must export the actual blow-up matrices and a bounded exact inverse/witness. The found blow-up cannot be imported as an unexplained all-width controller.

papers.title: Polynomial degree bounds for matrix semi-invariants
papers.reading_depth: abstract; Theorem 1.4 determinant invariants; Theorem 1.8 inspected
papers.locators: Theorems 1.4 and 1.8, PDF pp. 2-3; journal Advances in Mathematics 310, 44-63
papers.model: Left-right SL action, determinant blow-ups over infinite fields
papers.mapping: Finite blow-up degree bounds offer bounded exact searches for a fixed coefficient module. Their input dimension is the full module dimension, not the number of Gaussian calls.

papers.title: On non-commutative rank and tensor rank
papers.reading_depth: abstract; Example 1.1 elimination; tensor blow-up definitions and nonmonotonicity statements inspected
papers.model: Commutative versus free-skew-field rank; matrix-space blow-ups
papers.mapping: The skew 3-by-3 example becomes our explicit Pauli encoding. Fixed-size blow-up ranks need not increase monotonically, so a few successful finite tests cannot establish all widths.

papers.title: Degree bounds for semi-invariant rings of quivers
papers.reading_depth: abstract; path-pencil construction; Theorem 1.2; Section 7 proof and Section 8 discussion inspected
papers.model: Acyclic quiver representations with dimension vectors and determinant-character weights
papers.mapping: Type each register stage and each allowed coefficient map as arrows, then search only compatible encodings. Semi-invariant degree bounds certify a finite representation problem, not a native complexity bound.

papers.title: Relations between exact and approximate bilinear algorithms. Applications
papers.reading_depth: publisher abstract read; full text subscription blocked
papers.model: Approximate bilinear algorithms with an explicit error degree
papers.mapping: The abstract states an exactification cost factor 1+d. A local border construction therefore needs a complete interpolation invoice before it can improve the productive moment.

papers.authors: Dario Bini; Grazia Lotti; Francesco Romani
papers.title: Approximate Solutions for the Bilinear Form Computational Problem
papers.reading_depth: publisher abstract read through indexed primary result; direct refetch returned 403
papers.locators: Publisher abstract; SIAM Journal on Computing 9(4), 692-697
papers.model: Approximate bilinear forms and stability-aware complexity
papers.mapping: Approximation can lower multiplicative complexity while increasing numerical cost. No numeric stability statement is inferred here beyond the abstract; exact port bounds are proved independently.

papers.authors: James Demmel; Ioana Dumitriu; Olga Holtz; Robert Kleinberg
papers.title: Fast matrix multiplication is stable
papers.reading_depth: abstract; stationary error theorem and proof of exponent corollary inspected
papers.model: Recursive bilinear noncommutative matrix multiplication; normwise forward error
papers.mapping: Fixed certified coefficient families have polynomial error growth in dimension. Exponent existence does not choose an explicit fast family, and the theorem does not by itself analyze our Gaussian recursion.

papers.authors: Grey Ballard; Austin R. Benson; Alex Druinsky; Benjamin Lipshitz; Oded Schwartz
papers.title: Improving the numerical stability of fast matrix multiplication
papers.reading_depth: abstract; Definitions 1-2; Theorems 3/5 proof passages; diagonal-scaling Proposition 9 inspected
papers.locators: Definition 2 and Theorem 3, PDF pp. 7-11; Proposition 9, PDF p. 19
papers.model: Floating-point recursive bilinear multiplication; coefficient growth and input scaling
papers.mapping: Record coefficient magnitude and recursion error factors alongside operation counts. A smaller local conditioning constant may improve precision/constants without changing the multiplication exponent.

papers.title: The Clifford group, stabilizer states, and linear and quadratic operations over GF(2)
papers.reading_depth: abstract; Pauli multiplication and conjugation formulas; Theorems 1-3 inspected
papers.locators: Theorems 1-3, PDF pp. 2-3; Section III decomposition
papers.model: Binary symplectic/quadratic descriptions of Clifford conjugation
papers.mapping: Conjugation phases are indispensable, but conjugation still loses the absolute global scalar. Exact tensor-word synthesis must preserve that remaining scalar separately.

papers.title: Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits
papers.reading_depth: abstract; tableau operations; Lemma 5 proof; Theorem 8 canonical-form discussion inspected
papers.locators: Lemma 5 and Theorem 8, PDF pp. 9-10; v5 dated 18 June 2008
papers.model: Efficient classical simulation of Clifford/stabilizer circuits
papers.mapping: Tableau canonical forms can reduce duplicate discovery states. They cannot merge actual scalar-distinct linear maps in our ABI, and efficient quantum-circuit simulation does not mean a Gaussian array transform is free.

papers.title: Isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and cubic forms: completeness and reductions
papers.reading_depth: abstract; orbit-action taxonomy; Theorems A/B and Corollary B inspected
papers.locators: Section 3; Theorems A and B; Section 6.1
papers.model: Polynomial reductions among tensor/group/algebra isomorphism problems, with stated field restrictions
papers.mapping: Colored linear-algebra gadgets can encode register roles and forbid mixing incompatible endpoint types. Such reductions preserve isomorphism decisions rather than Gaussian-call or RAM-time complexity.

papers.authors: Vyacheslav Futorny; Joshua A. Grochow; Vladimir V. Sergeichuk
papers.title: Wildness for tensors
papers.reading_depth: abstract; Theorem 1.1; linked block-equivalence setup; Section 5 proof inspected
papers.model: Systems of order-at-most-three tensors and linked basis-change actions over arbitrary fields
papers.mapping: Its role-locking pattern can organize a typed controller search. The construction can grow with the number of parts and supplies no constant-cost runtime reduction for the multiplication algorithm.

papers.title: Triality, exceptional Lie algebras and Deligne dimension formulas
papers.reading_depth: abstract; Introduction; Section 2 triality definition and first model discussion inspected
papers.model: Characteristic-zero exceptional Lie algebras, composition algebras and D4 triality
papers.mapping: D4 triality is a specific relation among three eight-dimensional representations. Generic symplectic tensor-isomorphism padding is a different construction; a useful runtime transfer requires an explicit map into the current paid/free operators.
